title: Busy Shift Dinner Strategies
subtitle: Dinner when the board will not cooperate
description: Busy shift dinner strategies for fire stations: default meals, hold plans, and communication so food still happens when calls stack.
intro: Busy shift dinner is a strategy problem. You need a default meal everyone knows, a cook assigned early, and formats that survive pause. Waiting until 18:30 to 'see how the board looks' is how halls end up with nothing.

sections.heading: Default meals
paragraphs: Chili, quesadillas, sheet pan, pasta — rotate defaults monthly so shopping stays automatic.

sections.heading: Hold and communicate
paragraphs: Tell the crew when food is ready and what format — line at 18:30, not 'food sometime.' Holds on low beat reheating twelve individual plates after a call.

practicalAdvice: Pick dinner by 16:00 — adjust format, not whether you eat.
Keep a 30-minute fallback in the freezer.

mealRecommendations.title: Chili Mac Skillet
mealRecommendations.blurb: One pan — fast when the board stays loud.

faqs.question: Where do these recipes come from?
faqs.answer: Each link goes to a full recipe on Firehall Meals — crew-sized portions, station timing, and steps written for a shared kitchen. Not home-blog scaling.

faqs.question: What if crew size or time changes tonight?
faqs.answer: Use Find a Meal with your headcount and minutes available. It pulls from the same hall-tested dinners these guides recommend.
